items.component: Every form control (native form reset); in this cluster: TextField, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, NumberField, Slider, RangeSlider, Rating (Angular), ToggleGroup
items.summary: A native form reset becomes a value change made by the form in every adapter: afterwards each control holds, shows and submits its reset target and has notified once if and only if its value changed. One core listener serves the four adapters; Angular gains the mechanism in HwValueControl, React writes controlled props back to the DOM and Vue writes its model back.
verifiedBeforeSpecifying: React, jsdom, current tree: a controlled Select (value 'a', prompt) submits '' after form.reset() while the state stays 'a'; a controlled Checkbox (true) and Radio pair ('b') submit nothing / 'a' while the state stays true / 'b'. A component that re-renders once after the reset shows and submits the props again (React 19 rewrites checked, value and the selected option on every commit of the host element).

Chromium, trusted click and keyboard activation of a reset button: a microtask queued in a reset listener runs before the remaining listeners and before the browser resets the controls (it logged checked=true, value='typed'); with form.reset() or a scripted click it runs after the reset. The existing queueMicrotask pattern therefore reads stale values and cannot see a later preventDefault for real activations.

surface.react: No prop changes. Composite controls call onValueChange(target) once when the reset changed the value; controlled native controls (Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch) show their props again.
surface.vue: No prop changes. update:modelValue is emitted once, only when the reset changed the value.
surface.angular: No new inputs. Without an Angular Forms directive, (valueChange) emits the initial value after a native reset that changed the value. Protected hooks for subclasses: afterReset(), syncDom().
surface.vanilla: RangeSlider, ToggleGroup and Rating controllers dispatch hw:change with detail.value and call onValueChange after a reset that changed the value.

endState.dom: No element or attribute changes. After a reset the native controls carry the reset target as properties (value, checked, selected) and hidden inputs carry it as value.
endState.behaviour: Reset target: React and Vue `defaultValue` (or the matching default prop), else the empty value ('', [], false, null, the Slider midpoint (min + max) / 2, the RangeSlider [min, max]). Angular: with Angular Forms attached (registerOnChange was called) the component changes no value itself and only writes what it holds to the DOM; otherwise the value held after the first ngOnInit. Vanilla: the authored values captured when the controller is created. Read-only and disabled controls are reset too; a default-prevented reset changes nothing. Timing: onReset runs after the browser has reset the form's controls: in the same microtask checkpoint when the reset came from script (form.reset(), a scripted click), and before the next paint (first of requestAnimationFrame and a zero timeout) when the reader activated a reset button. Server rendering: no listener is attached on the server; React attaches in an effect, Vue in onMounted, Angular in afterNextRender, vanilla when the controller is created.

core.signature: observeFormReset(control: Element, onReset: () => void): { destroy(): void }
core.behaviour: New file core/src/form-reset.ts, exported from core/src/index.ts after line 204. Adds one capture listener for `reset` on the control's root (control.getRootNode(), else the owner document): the document, the shadow root when the control is inside one, or, for a tree that is not connected yet, that tree's root together with the owner document (one event is handled once). Returns a no-op observer when the root cannot listen. At event time the owning form is resolved, so the `form` attribute, a later association and a moved control are honoured without re-subscribing: control.form when the control matches `input, select, textarea, button, output`, else the form of the first `input, select, textarea` inside it, else control.closest('form'); events of other forms are ignored. Then queueMicrotask: when event.eventPhase is 0 the dispatch is over and the browser has already reset the controls: call onReset unless event.defaultPrevented. Otherwise the event is still being dispatched (trusted activation): wait for the first of view.requestAnimationFrame and view.setTimeout(0) (run once), then call onReset unless defaultPrevented. Nothing runs after destroy(). No module-level browser global.
Object.is(a, b), or both are arrays of equal length whose entries are pairwise Object.is. Used for the 'notify only when the value changed' rule.

conventionConflicts.conflict: The rule says 'one microtask after a reset event'. Measured in Chromium: when the reader clicks or presses Enter on a reset button, a microtask queued in a reset listener runs before the remaining listeners and before the browser resets the controls; only form.reset() and scripted clicks run it afterwards.
conventionConflicts.closest: observeFormReset calls onReset in that microtask when the dispatch is over (event.eventPhase === 0) and otherwise before the next paint (first of requestAnimationFrame and a zero timeout). (a)-(d) of the rule hold from that moment. Tests that reset from script still see the result after one awaited microtask; RESET-12 covers the real activation in the browser suite.
conventionConflicts.affects: All five clusters: nobody may add a reset listener of their own or assume microtask timing.

conventionConflicts.conflict: 'Select without defaultValue resets to the option the browser selects after the reset, read from the element' cannot be applied: Vue renders the `selected` attribute from the live model (verified), so the browser's reset re-selects the current option.
conventionConflicts.closest: The target is computed from the element's option list: the first option that is not disabled, which is what a native select without a selected attribute shows.
